subject: history
topicName: Women and the Family in Nazi Germany

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Nazi ideal for women was summed up as the "Three Ks" - Kinder, Küche, Kirche (Children, Kitchen, Church). Hitler believed that a woman's proper place was in the home, producing Aryan children and supporting her husband. He said: "The woman is the eternal companion of the man, and her world is the family."

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: In June 1933, the Law for the Encouragement of Marriage offered marriage loans of 1,000 marks to young couples if the wife gave up her job. For each child born, 25% of the loan was cancelled. If a couple had four children, the entire loan was wiped out.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Nazis introduced several policies to push women out of professional employment. In 1933, women in the civil service, medicine, and teaching were dismissed or encouraged to resign. By 1936, women were barred from legal professions and from being judges. The number of women at university was limited to 10% of enrolments.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Despite Nazi ideology, the number of women in employment actually INCREASED during the 1930s. By 1937, there were more women in work than when Hitler came to power. The reality was that Germany's economic recovery and rearmament programme needed workers, and many families needed a second income. The gap between Nazi ideology and economic reality was significant.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two ways the Nazis encouraged women to have more children. (4 marks) | How far did Nazi policies improve the lives of German women? (8 marks) | "The Nazis failed to control women's employment." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: The Three Ks (Kinder, Küche, Kirche) is the starting point for any answer about Nazi women's policy Know the specific policies: Marriage Loans (June 1933), Mother's Cross (August 1938), 10% university limit The employment statistics show the CONTRADICTION in Nazi policy - more women worked in 1939 than 1933 Always distinguish between Nazi IDEOLOGY (women at home) and REALITY (women needed at work) The birth rate rose but never matched Weimar levels and was falling by 1939 - Nazi policies were not fully successful Forced sterilisation of 320,000 women is crucial evidence that Nazi policy was coercive, not just encouraging Link the war to the failure of Nazi ideology - the state needed women workers and abandoned its own principles
